verses.text: News reached the apostles and believers across Judea: Gentiles had received God’s message too. 🌍
When Peter got back to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers challenged him.
They said, “You went into the home of uncircumcised men and even ate with them!”
So Peter laid it all out for them, step by step:
“I was praying in Joppa when I saw a vision while in a trance: something like a huge sheet came down from heaven, lowered by its four corners, and stopped right in front of me.
I looked closely. Inside were land animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
Then I heard a voice say, ‘Get up, Peter. Kill and eat!’
I said, ‘No way, Lord! Nothing unclean or impure has ever gone into my mouth.’
But the voice answered from heaven a second time: ‘Don’t call unclean what God has made clean.’
This happened three times, then everything was pulled back up into heaven.
Right then, three men sent from Caesarea arrived at the house where I was staying.
The Spirit told me to go with them without hesitation. These six brothers came with me too, and we entered the man’s home.
He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house, saying, ‘Send to Joppa and bring Simon, also called Peter.
He’ll tell you words through which you and everyone in your household will be saved.’
As I began speaking, the Holy Spirit came down on them, just as the Spirit came on us at the beginning.
Then I remembered what the Lord had said: ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
So if God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to stand in God’s way?”
When they heard this, they had nothing more to say. They praised God: “So God has given the Gentiles the chance to turn back and receive life too!”
After Stephen’s persecution scattered the believers, some traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They shared God’s message with Jews only.
But some believers from Cyprus and Cyrene came to Antioch and began telling Greek-speaking people the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord’s power was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
News about this reached the Jerusalem church, so they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When he arrived and saw what God’s grace had done, he was glad. He encouraged everyone to stay close to the Lord with all their heart.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. Many more people came to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
When he found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met with the church and taught many people. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
Around that time, prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, Agabus, stood up and, through the Spirit, warned that a severe famine would spread across the whole Roman world. It happened during Claudius’s reign.
So the disciples decided to send help to the believers in Judea, each according to what they could afford.
They did it, sending their support to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
